newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy minister says Albania police must be neutral.
newsitem.headline: Italy minister says Albania police must be neutral.

text.p: Italian Deputy Defence Minister Massimo Brutti on Monday urged Albania to make sure its police force was non-political and said his country could supply equipment to help the police force.

Brutti arrived in Albania on a one-day visit and toured the southern port town of Vlore, the epicentre of the riots and disorder that convulsed Albania in February and March after the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Italy has taken key role in solving the Albanian crisis and leads a U.N.-backed force that is securing the supply of aid.
"There is a need for a police force which does not obey any of the parties and is neutral and credible," Brutti told a news conference.
"We are giving this assistance for the police because we think that building an efficent police force in this country is an urgent objective," he added.
Some Albanian politicians have said the police force is under the control of the former ruling Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha.
Brutti said his country could supply the police with equipment such as radios and training.
"The (international) military force cannot take the place of the Albanian police," he added.
